title: Jev World
description: A playable world: its state, the judgements made about it, and the rules deciding what happens. See ABOUT-THE-GAME.md for the design this generalises.

schemaVersion.description: Format version. The engine refuses any other, so a future change cannot be misread.

goal.description: One line telling the player what they are trying to do.

examples.description: Shown at the start, so the player has somewhere to begin.

stateTemplate.description: How the state is described to the model. Placeholders are state field keys. Every placeholder must name a declared field, or the model is sent a literal '{{has_keys}}'.

describe.description: How this field reads in the state description, keyed by value. A bool must describe both 'true' and 'false'; an int or text may use '*' as a fallback sentence.

judgements.description: One API question per entry, all asked in a single call.

kind.description: noul is a probability, choice is one of a named set, score is a position on an ordered scale.

question.description: The instruction sent to the model. Must use {{action}}. Wording is behaviour: see README.md for two measured cases where rephrasing made a world unplayable.

fallback.description: Used when the model returns nothing usable. For a choice or score it must match a declared option or level.

description.description: What the option means, in the player's likely vocabulary. A bare name classifies far worse than a described one.

levels.description: Ordered levels for a score judgement.

rules.description: Evaluated in order; the first whose condition holds is applied.

condition.description: Exactly one comparison, or exactly one combinator. Mixing forms is rejected: a condition that can express anything is a programming language, and a world author should be writing data.

atLeast.description: Holds when the value is at or above this.

below.description: Holds when the value is below this.

equals.description: Holds when the value is this. Named 'equals' on the wire; the C# member is Matches so it does not shadow object.Equals.

roll.description: A probability compared against a roll of the dice. This is how a world uses a probability as a probability rather than as a threshold.

chance.description: A fixed chance, when no judgement supplies one.

atLeast.description: A floor the chance must clear before a roll is made, so a hopeless attempt stays hopeless on a lucky roll.

scale.description: Scales the chance, so a roll can be made harder or easier.

state.description: The field to change, for set and increment.

to.description: The value to set, interpreted against the field's declared type.

by.description: How much to add, for increment.

text.description: The line to print, for narrate.
